variant_audit.question: Does R02/R05 repeat the R01 defect of stating S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition behaviour as a general SAP PS rule?
variant_audit.answer: Yes, but at far lower incidence than R01 (V01 found 18 in R01). 24 records in this pair are sourced from S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition documentation (R02-059..R02-072, R05-076..R05-094 minus on-prem API records). Most are explicitly scoped in claim_text with "In SAP S/4HANA Cloud" or "cloud" or a cloud-only object name. Four are not, and of those, three are genuine variant-mixing defects that would become wrong universal rules (R02-060, R02-061, R02-065, R02-072 - downgraded to OVERSTATED). R02-067, R02-069 and R02-071 are unscoped but independently corroborated for on-premise/ECC by other sources in the same lane, so they were not downgraded.
variant_audit.most_serious: R02-072. The page states verbatim "This is the standard way of granting authorizations in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition" immediately before the quoted restriction-field list, and the same lane pair separately documents the completely different on-premise mechanism (PFCG authorization objects C_PROJ_*/C_PRPS_*, R05-066/R05-067). Carrying R02-072 forward unscoped would put two mutually exclusive authorization models into the blueprint as if they were one.

org_field_audit.mandatory: VERIFIED against the Organizational Assignments topic re-fetched at the recorded URL (S/4HANA on-premise 2025 FPS01). Project definition: Controlling Area = Required, (Object) Currency = Required, Company code = Required, Business area = Required only if business area balances are managed in the company code, Profit Center = Optional, Plant = Optional. WBS element: Controlling Area = Display, Currency = Required, Company code = Required, Business area = conditional, Profit Center = Optional, Plant = Optional, Object Class = "Required value for new WBS elements".
org_field_audit.inherited: VERIFIED. Controlling area is "Inherited by any new elements your create or insert into the WBS". Org values are copied from the project definition when WBS elements are created or incorporated. Inheritance is copy-on-create, NOT a live reference: "If you change the project definition later, the changes have no effect on the values taken from the project definition and inserted into existing WBS elements." Same one-shot semantics apply from project profile to project definition.
org_field_audit.frozen: VERIFIED. Controlling area on the project definition is frozen at first save (exception: standard WBS). Company code, business area and object currency on a WBS element are frozen once plan/actual values, commitments or budget exist. Object class and the integrated planning indicator are changeable only until plan or actual values exist. Statistical key figure frozen once plan or actual values exist. Functional area is frozen once postings exist (separate source, R02-080). Network header controlling area and company code are Display and are determined when the plant is created.
org_field_audit.correction: The only mutability/mandatory defect found is R02-094, which silently added functional area to the mandatory/optional taxonomy drawn from a page that never mentions functional area.

status_forbids_audit.finding: The "what a status forbids" records survive verification, but with three precision caveats the blueprint must carry.
caveats: CLSD on a WBS element prohibits posting actual costs TO THE WBS ELEMENT and prohibits assigning networks/production orders/CO orders to it - but it explicitly still ALLOWS posting actual costs to orders and networks already assigned to that WBS element, as long as their own status permits (R05-020 + R05-021 read together). "Cannot post" is therefore not absolute at the subtree level.
Network CLSD is stricter than WBS CLSD: it "Prevents you making actual postings, for instance, confirmations" outright (R05-054).

The evidence quote chosen for R05-020 is not discriminating - the identical sentence "You from assigning networks, production orders or CO orders to the WBS element." occurs three times on the SAP page, and under REL and TECO it is filed under "The status allows". SAP's own allows/prohibits rendering under REL and TECO is corrupted. Do not re-derive this rule from the quote alone.
REL on a network is a necessary but not sufficient condition for creating reservations/purchase requisitions: SAP qualifies it with "depending on settings elsewhere" (R05-048, downgraded).
DLFL's settled-balance precondition is defeasible by Customizing (the "Must not be settled" indicator in the settlement profile), so it is a configurable gate, not a hard one (R05-026, downgraded).
